reuse.why: Every inline midpoint copy (forecast normaliser, updateActions, postTransactionForSchedule, preview transactions, schedule template) is replaced by a call to the existing shared getScheduledAmount, and the approximate tolerance comes from the existing getApproxNumberThreshold.

duplication.why: It removes five duplicated copies of the expected-amount rule, leaving one definition.

placement.why: The rule lives in shared/schedules.ts and is consumed by the server, API model and client layers through imports.

scope.why: The edits all serve the expected-amount rule and API field. The UI display sites that also call the helper are left without the operator, which is reasonable but uneven.

maintainability.why: There is one small, well-tested definition, but adding the operator after the boolean `inverse` forces `getScheduledAmount(x, false, op)` with a bare positional false at every call site.

bypasses_abstraction.where: After the change no site re-implements the amount rule. All go through getScheduledAmount.

abstraction_drift.where: getScheduledAmount in packages/loot-core/src/shared/schedules.ts gains an `op` parameter and an isapprox branch, which is the real variation the steps ask for. No call site re-implements it, though SchedulesTable, the mobile list and useScheduleEdit call it without the operator.
